title: Last-vertex simplex resolution preserves cocone spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets, constant diagrams and right-pinched Kan mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with universes enlarged as necessary. For a small simplicial set $X$, let $\mathsf S(X)$ be the ordinary category whose objects are all simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$, including degenerate simplices, and whose morphisms $\sigma\to\tau$ are monotone maps $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with $\tau\Delta(\alpha)=\sigma$; composition is composition of the monotone maps. Define $\ell_X:N(\mathsf S(X))\to X$ on a chain $\sigma_0\to\cdots\to\sigma_r$, with $\sigma_i:\Delta^{n_i}\to X$, by applying $\sigma_r$ to the simplex of $\Delta^{n_r}$ whose $i$th vertex is the image of $n_i$ under the composite $[n_i]\to[n_r]$. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, every map $p:X\to\mathcal E$ and every vertex $T\in\mathcal E$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_XT)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathsf S(X)),\mathcal E)}(p\ell_X,\Delta_{N(\mathsf S(X))}T).$$
No quasicategory hypothesis on $X$ and no colimit-existence hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ is imposed. The assertion includes $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: HTT Proposition 4.2.3.14 and its last-vertex construction in Lemma 4.2.3.13, printed pp. 254-255; Proposition 4.1.1.7, printed p. 226, for the fiberwise cocone assertion; compare the natural join/cocone equivalence of lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison. Online primary source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag is asserted.

proof.text: Put $I=\mathsf S(X)$ and define $F:I\to\mathrm{sSet}_{/X}$ by $F(\tau:\Delta^m\to X)=(\Delta^m,\tau)$ and $F(\alpha)=\Delta(\alpha)$. The arrow equation in the statement makes this a functor over $X$. All its sets are small: its objects are the countable union of the sets $X_m$, and arrows are subsets of the corresponding sets of finite monotone maps. Use the explicit construction in [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones] to form $H=X_F$, with inclusions $b:X\hookrightarrow H$ and $a:N(I)\hookrightarrow H$ and the specified maps $\iota_\tau:(\Delta^m)^{\triangleright}\to H$. In a mixed $r$-simplex write its cut as $i$, its upper chain as $\tau_{i+1}\to\cdots\to\tau_r$, with $\tau_j:\Delta^{m_j}\to X$, and its compatible lifts as $u_j:[i]\to[m_j]$. Thus the lower simplex is $\tau_j\Delta(u_j)$. The cases $i=-1$ and $i=r$ are respectively the pure nerve and pure $X$ cases.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1, pp. 248-249, specialized as immediately before Lemma 4.2.3.13, p. 254.

proof.text: Construct $r:H\to X$. It is the identity on pure $X$ simplices. If an upper block is present, form $v:[r]\to[m_r]$ by $v(k)=u_r(k)$ for $k\leq i$ and, for $k>i$, by taking the image of $m_k$ under the tail composite $[m_k]\to[m_r]$; set $r(e)=\tau_r\Delta(v)$. This is monotone: lower values are at most the image of $m_{i+1}$, and successive upper values increase because each monotone map sends its last vertex to a vertex at most the next last vertex. Here is the operator check, including the nontrivial case of removing the last object. For a monotone $\theta:[s]\to[r]$ retaining an upper vertex, let $c:[m_{\theta(s)}]\to[m_r]$ be the tail composite. The formula for the restricted simplex gives $cv'=v\theta$, and its terminal structural simplex is $\tau_{\theta(s)}=\tau_r\Delta(c)$. If no upper vertex is retained, $v\theta=u_r\theta$ and the restricted simplex is exactly the lower simplex. If no lower vertex is retained, the same tail-composite formula applies without the $u_j$ terms. Repeated vertices use identity arrows, so the calculation also covers degeneracies. These equations prove that $r$ is simplicial. They also show $rb=\mathrm{id}_X$, $ra=\ell_X$ exactly, and that $r\iota_\tau:\Delta^{m+1}\to X$ is $\tau$ composed with the order map $[m+1]\to[m]$ fixing $0,\ldots,m$ and repeating $m$ at the last vertex.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.3.13 and the definition of the cofinal map in Proposition 4.2.3.14, p. 254; operator check written out.

proof.text: Fix $p:X\to\mathcal E$ and $T\in\mathcal E_0$, and put $q=pr$. For every $\tau:\Delta^m\to X$, the preceding formula identifies $q\iota_\tau$ with the specified repeat-last-vertex cocone on $p\tau$. By the standard-simplex clause of [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit], this particular cocone is colimiting with vertex $p\tau(m)$. Thus every hypothesis of [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones] holds for $F$ and $q$: the index is a small ordinary category, its maps to $X$ are allowed to be noninjective, and each of the required local colimits has just been produced. It gives an equivalence $b^*:C_H\to C_X$, where $C_H=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(H,\mathcal E)}(q,\Delta_HT)$ and $C_X=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_XT)$. No colimit of $p$ itself was assumed or used.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.4, pp. 249-251, applied in the final paragraph of Proposition 4.2.3.14, p. 255.

proof.text: Precomposition with $r$ defines $r^*:C_X\to C_H$ because $q=pr$ and constant diagrams remain constant. The equation $rb=\mathrm{id}_X$ gives $b^*r^*=\mathrm{id}_{C_X}$ strictly, in every simplicial degree of the right-pinched mapping spaces. Since $b^*$ is an equivalence of Kan complexes by step 3, $r^*$ is an equivalence: the equation on components makes its component map the inverse bijection, and for every basepoint the same equation makes its homotopy-group maps inverse isomorphisms. This also covers empty cocone spaces, since the component bijection forces both spaces to be empty together.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.14, final paragraph, p. 255; the retraction argument in the precise fixed-apex mapping-space form.

proof.text: We check the simplex-lift hypotheses of [lem-coef-decomposition-simplex-lift-right-anodyne]. For $z:\Delta^n\to X$, identify $I_z$ explicitly with the category of factorizations $z=\tau\Delta(s)$, with $s:[n]\to[m]$, $\tau:\Delta^m\to X$. Its arrows $(s,\tau)\to(s',\tau')$ are monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[m']$ satisfying $s'=\alpha s$ and $\tau=\tau'\Delta(\alpha)$. The object $(\mathrm{id}_{[n]},z)$ is initial: its unique arrow to $(s,\tau)$ is $s$. The unique arrows from it give a natural transformation from the constant functor at that object to the identity. By [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence], projection $N(I_z)\to\Delta^0$ is a homotopy equivalence on realization. In particular the contractibility condition holds for every nondegenerate $z$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.14, first part of proof, p. 254: the initial object of the simplex-factorization category.

proof.text: Now suppose $z$ is degenerate. The lift of $z$ in the value $\Delta^m$ is precisely the monotone map $s:[n]\to[m]$, and it is degenerate if and only if $s$ is noninjective: factor $s=j_s q_s$ into its surjection onto its ordered image and the injection of that image; a proper surjection gives a degeneracy, whereas a map factoring through a proper surjection cannot be injective. Thus $D_z$ consists of factorizations with $s$ noninjective. Let $B_z\subseteq D_z$ be the full subcategory where $s$ is also surjective. Define $R:D_z\to B_z$ by $(s,\tau)\mapsto(q_s,\tau\Delta(j_s))$, keeping the canonical increasing enumeration of each finite image. For an arrow $\alpha$ as above, $\alpha$ maps the image of $s$ onto the image of $s'$; it induces a unique monotone $\beta$ with $\alpha j_s=j_{s'}\beta$ and $\beta q_s=q_{s'}$. This is the required arrow between the two images under $R$, since $\tau\Delta(j_s)=\tau'\Delta(j_{s'})\Delta(\beta)$. Uniqueness gives identity and composition laws. Writing $J:B_z\hookrightarrow D_z$, one has $RJ=\mathrm{id}$, and $j_s$ gives a natural transformation $JR\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}_{D_z}$. By [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence], $N(J)$ and $N(R)$ are inverse up to homotopy. This proves the deformation-retract assertion with its maps and arrow direction specified.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.14, p. 255: the subcategory denoted I-double-prime and its right-adjoint image-factorization retraction; details supplied.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], write $z=\bar z\Delta(t)$ uniquely with $\bar z:\Delta^d\to X$ nondegenerate and $t:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[d]$ surjective. Since $z$ is degenerate, $d<n$, so $(t,\bar z)$ belongs to $B_z$. It is terminal there. Indeed, for an object $(s,\tau)$ with $s$ surjective, decompose $\tau=\rho\Delta(u)$ with $u$ surjective and $\rho$ nondegenerate. Uniqueness applied to $z=\rho\Delta(us)$ gives $\rho=\bar z$ and $us=t$. Thus $u$ defines an arrow $(s,\tau)\to(t,\bar z)$. This arrow is unique because $s$ is surjective. The terminal-object arrows define a natural transformation from the identity of $B_z$ to its constant terminal functor; [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] makes $N(B_z)$ weakly contractible. Together with step 6, $N(D_z)$ is weakly contractible. Step 5 also gives weak contractibility of $N(I_z)$. Therefore $N(D_z)\hookrightarrow N(I_z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: both have one component and all their homotopy groups vanish, so the induced component and homotopy-group maps are isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.14, p. 255: terminal nondegenerate factorization in I-double-prime; Eilenberg-Zilber uniqueness and the degenerate-lift comparison.

proof.text: Steps 5-7 verify both hypotheses of [lem-coef-decomposition-simplex-lift-right-anodyne] for the actual diagram $F(\tau)=(\Delta^m,\tau)$. Hence $a:N(I)\hookrightarrow H$ is right anodyne. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] with this inclusion, the quasicategory $\mathcal E$, the diagram $q=pr$ and the fixed apex $T$. It gives an equivalence $a^*:C_H\to C_I$, where $C_I=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal E)}(p\ell_X,\Delta_{N(I)}T)$, using $qa=pra=p\ell_X$. The cited theorem permits an arbitrary simplicial target for the inclusion, so no quasicategory assertion about $H$ or $X$ has entered the proof.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.8, p. 252, and Proposition 4.2.3.14, pp. 254-255; the fixed-apex restriction assertion uses Proposition 4.1.1.7, p. 226.

proof.text: The strict equation $ra=\ell_X$ gives $\ell_X^*=a^*r^*$, with the mapping spaces and restricted diagrams exactly as in the statement. Step 4 proves $r^*$ an equivalence, and step 8 proves $a^*$ an equivalence; their composite is an equivalence on components and every based homotopy group. This proves the assertion for every $p,\mathcal E,T$. If $X=\varnothing$, its simplex category is empty and $H=\varnothing$ by the explicit construction, so $\ell_X$ and the displayed restriction are identity maps; the argument includes this case without requiring an object of the empty index category. Only the standard-simplex local colimits of step 3 were used, so no ambient colimit-existence assumption is added.

source.place: Conclusion of Proposition 4.2.3.14, with the natural fixed-apex comparisons of Proposition 4.1.1.7 and the join/cocone convention, pp. 226,254-255.

lean.statement: theorem simplex_last_vertex_cocone_equivalence (X E : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory E] (p : X ⟶ E) (T : E _⦋0⦌) : KanComplex (mappingSpace ((ihom X).obj E) (diagramVertex p) ((constantDiagrams X E).app _ T)) ∧ KanComplex (mappingSpace ((ihom (nerve (simplexCategory X))).obj E) (diagramVertex (simplexCategoryLastVertex X ≫ p)) ((constantDiagrams (nerve (simplexCategory X)) E).app _ T)) ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (mappingSpaceMap ((MonoidalClosed.pre (simplexCategoryLastVertex X)).app E) (diagramVertex p) ((constantDiagrams X E).app _ T))
